name: Cliff Bentz

gaps: No campaign website listed in the voters' pamphlet statement; none confirmed via T1/T3
collection_notes: Steps 1-5 were run identically for every candidate in the US Senate, US House 1-6 and Governor races (the shared WebSearch budget ran out once mid-run and the remaining searches were completed after it reset). To keep effort equal, no T3 items are included for any candidate in these races: every item comes from the T1 voters' pamphlet, official .gov pages or official roll-call pages; promising T3 results are named in these notes for possible later, race-wide use. Campaign websites are recorded from the pamphlet but were not fetched for positions, for any candidate. oregonlive.com and apnews.com are rejected by the search proxy as allowed_domains, so step 5 used three fixed domain groups for everyone: (opb, oregoncapitalchronicle, wweek, ballotpedia), (kgw, koin, kptv, katu), (portlandmercury, vote411, pamplinmedia, portlandtribune). The Multnomah military/overseas online voters' guide was checked and contains no federal or governor statements. Pamphlet excerpts were obtained through a summarizing fetch limited to ~125-character quotes, so excerpts are short. Incumbency: pamphlet occupation 'U.S. Congressman' with '(2021-present)' and bentz.house.gov. Search results show cliffbentz.com, but it is not linked from the pamphlet and was not confirmed via a T1/T3 link, so website_url is null. The Save America / Secure America vote claims (p4) are his own pamphlet wording; roll calls for those were not fetched. Promising general-election T3 items exist for both candidates (OPB 2026-09-30 'Chris Beck puts rural health care at the center of his race against Cliff Bentz'; KOIN 'Cliff Bentz shares his stance on key issues ahead of midterms') but were not fetched, to keep T3 treatment identical across all assigned races.
